name: Lamet

anatomy.part: crown of the kite, the top apex of the diamond body
left wing tip of the kite, the end of the cross-spar
centre of the cross-spar, where the spar crosses the spine just below the crown
lower-left edge of the kite body, on the lower-left seam between the left wing tip and the lower corner
lower corner of the kite, the point where the tail hangs from
the name-knot, the bottom of the tail where the name-strip and the ribbon are tied
tip of the tapered name-strip, hanging down and to the left
tip of the ribbon flutter, branching to the right from the name-knot

myth: When old Tenu went aloft, his grandchildren sewed his name onto a strip of sailcloth, one knot for each letter. They flew it at midsummer, when the light stays late. Ennu the Kite-Wright had built the frame, and Aun had shown him how to bend it, the way Aun shows everyone things, without asking first. The name-kite climbs the Lamp Road with its tail behind, so every star that sees it knows who is passing. Tavo came over the north ridge to tear the strip, because Tavo laughs at names and cannot be bargained with. The children held the reel and sang. Hesk, at the pole, did not look up. She keeps count. She marks each name as it passes her string and lets none of them go. The strip is knotted to the bright star at the tail, and that is where the name stays when the cloth wears thin. So we tie our names on. The wind does not read. Hesk does.
verse:
A cloth strip climbs slow
up the road; Hesk keeps the name
one knot in the wind
